introduction_section.heading: What is
content: Digital Product Design goes far beyond just making screens look pretty. It is the holistic process of identifying a market opportunity, defining the core problem, and crafting a comprehensive software solution (like a SaaS platform or complex mobile app) that delivers immense value to both the user and the business.

At Devisgon, we act as your strategic product partners. We guide you through discovery, market validation, MVP (Minimum Viable Product) definition, and full-scale UI/UX design. We ensure that what we build together is not only highly usable but also commercially viable and technically feasible.
introduction_section.highlight_quote: “Design is not just what it looks like. Design is how it works and why it matters.”

faq_section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_section.subtitle: Get answers about product strategy and design

questions.question: What is the difference between UI/UX and Product Design?
questions.answer: While UI/UX focuses primarily on the user journey and the visual interface of the software, Product Design is broader. It encompasses UI/UX but also deeply integrates business strategy, market validation, monetization, and feature prioritization.

questions.question: What is an MVP?
questions.answer: MVP stands for Minimum Viable Product. It is the absolute leanest version of your product that still solves the core problem for your users. We focus heavily on defining the MVP so you can launch faster, gather real data, and avoid wasting money on features users don't need.

questions.question: How long does the Product Design phase take?
questions.answer: Depending on the complexity of the platform, a full product design cycle (from initial discovery to developer-ready prototypes) typically takes between 4 to 8 weeks.

questions.question: Do you also build and code the product?
questions.answer: Yes! Once the product design and prototyping phase is complete and approved by you, we seamlessly hand off the blueprints to our in-house engineering team to develop the frontend and backend of the application.
